question: Should the Claws package lifecycle become a core persistent owner of globally shared `mcp.servers` declarations, or should packages use the existing bundle-style plugin and MCP management surfaces?
rationale: The code can implement either model safely, but only maintainers can establish the durable product, trust, coexistence, and upgrade contract while the governing RFC and prerequisite stack remain open.

options.title: Defer until RFC acceptance
options.body: Keep this draft open and unmerged until the RFC explicitly approves the core ownership boundary and its coexistence and trust contracts.

options.title: Approve core Claw ownership
options.body: Accept the new core ledger after current-head live proof demonstrates safe fresh install, coexistence, reconciliation, drift, export, and cleanup.

options.title: Use bundle-style plugin ownership
options.body: Rework MCP packaging through the preferred plugin surface if the RFC cannot establish a distinct missing core capability.

recommendation.title: Defer until RFC acceptance
recommendation.body: Keep this draft open and unmerged until the RFC explicitly approves the core ownership boundary and its coexistence and trust contracts.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned, supplied the concrete boundary review, and are the strongest visible product-model owner for this stack.
